section.content: 本发明涉及一种调节器用半导体集成电路设置有：打开异常检测电路，其检测输出端子的打开状态；短路异常检测电路，其检测短路状态；第一输出端子，其用于将打开异常检测电路的检测结果输出给外部；第二输出端子，其用于将短路异常检测电路的检测结果输出给外部；和过热保护电路，其检测出半导体基板的温度，在检测出基板温度上升到预先设定的预定温度以上时，断开电压控制用晶体管，该调节器用半导体集成电路通过第二输出端子输出取过热保护电路的输出信号与短路异常检测电路的输出信号的逻辑或的信号，不会根据上述过热保护电路的输出信号来阻止打开异常检测电路的输出信号。

The invention relates to a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator, comprising: an opening abnormality detection circuit that detects an open state of the output terminal; a short-circuit abnormality detection circuit that detects a short-circuit state; a first output terminal for outputting a detection result of the opening abnormality detection circuit to the outside; a second output terminal for outputting a detection result of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit to the outside; and an overheat protection circuit for detecting a temperature of the semiconductor substrate and turning off the voltage control transistor when the temperature of the substrate is detected to be higher than a predetermined temperature set in advance, wherein the regulator semiconductor integrated circuit outputs a signal obtained by logically or the output signal of the overheat protection circuit and the output signal of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit through a second output terminal, and does not prevent the output signal of the open abnormality detection circuit from being turned on in accordance with the output signal of the overheat protection circuit.

Semiconductor integrated circuit for regulatorTechnical Field

The present invention relates to an effective technique used in a semiconductor integrated circuit (regulator IC) constituting a voltage regulator such as a series regulator that further converts a dc voltage in a dc power supply device.

Background

A series regulator (hereinafter, abbreviated as a regulator) is a power supply device that controls a transistor provided between a dc voltage input terminal and an output terminal and outputs a dc voltage of a desired potential. As an application of the regulator, there is a power supply device (vehicle-mounted regulator) for supplying a direct-current power supply to a vehicle-mounted electronic device such as a navigation device, an ETC device, an audio device, and an antenna device of a vehicle.

In general, in an in-vehicle regulator, an in-vehicle electronic device such as a navigation device is connected to the regulator through a connector. Therefore, the vibration connector of the vehicle body is disengaged, the output terminal of the power supply is opened, and a short circuit occurs in the electronic device as a load. Therefore, a function of detecting such an abnormal state in the regulator for vehicle mounting is demanded. Further, there is also a demand for a function of preventing a main apparatus from being damaged by an excessive current flowing when a receiving antenna is connected such as GPS, VICS (registered trademark), radio broadcasting, and the like.

Therefore, as shown in fig. 5, for example, there is proposed a configuration in which a resistor for current detection (a detection resistor R1) is provided on the input terminal side of the regulator, a dc voltage from the battery is supplied via the detection resistor, a personal computer for control is provided, the terminal voltage of the detection resistor is input to the personal computer, and the personal computer can detect opening and short-circuiting of the output terminal of the regulator by software processing (patent document 1).

Further, an invention has been proposed in which a dc voltage from a battery is supplied to an input terminal of a regulator via a detection resistor, an overcurrent protection circuit including an amplifier for amplifying a voltage between terminals of the detection resistor and a comparator for comparing an output of the amplifier with a reference voltage is provided, and the overcurrent protection circuit is operated when an output terminal is short-circuited to control a transistor for controlling an output voltage to limit a current, thereby preventing an overcurrent (patent document 2).

Further, an invention of a semiconductor device is disclosed (patent document 3) including an overheat protection circuit, and when the overheat protection circuit detects overheat of the substrate, the operation of the internal power supply generation circuit is stopped.

Patent document 1: japanese laid-open patent publication No. 2012-93296

Patent document 2: japanese patent laid-open publication No. 2015-5171

Patent document 3: japanese patent laid-open publication No. 2013-102603

Disclosure of Invention

In the invention described in patent document 1, the personal computer determines whether the output terminal of the regulator is open or short-circuited, and therefore there is a problem that the load on the personal computer is increased.

In both of the inventions described in patent document 1 and patent document 2, a detection resistor is provided at an input terminal of the regulator, a current flowing in an output terminal is converted into a voltage, and opening and short-circuiting of a load connected to the output terminal are detected. Therefore, excessive power consumption occurs in the detection resistor.

Further, although there is a regulator IC provided with an overheat protection circuit, there is no regulator IC provided with an open-abnormality detection circuit, and there is no regulator IC provided with an open-abnormality detection circuit and an overheat protection circuit.

The present inventors have studied a regulator IC including a turn-on abnormality detection circuit and an overheat protection circuit. As a result, in the case of a configuration in which the opening abnormality detection circuit detects a decrease in the output current and detects an abnormality, the overheat protection circuit operates to reduce the output current, and it is determined that the opening abnormality detection circuit operates and an opening abnormality occurs, and a detection signal is output.

Therefore, at this time, a logic gate such as an AND gate is provided which turns off the detection signal of the opening abnormality detection circuit by its output if the overheat protection circuit is operating, AND as shown in fig. 6, when the output TSD of the opening abnormality detection circuit rises (during a high level period), the detection signal Err _ OP of the opening abnormality detection circuit is generally not present (the detection level is not changed) (see a portion surrounded by a chain line denoted by a in fig. 6).

Further, when the regulator IC is provided with an open abnormality detection circuit and an overheat protection circuit in addition to the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit originally provided, external terminals for outputting respective signals are generally provided to notify the operation of these circuits to the outside, which leads to a problem that the number of external terminals increases and the chip size increases.

The present invention has been made in view of the above-described problems, and an object of the present invention is to provide a semiconductor integrated circuit (regulator IC) constituting a dc power supply device such as a series regulator, in which, when an abnormality detection circuit for detecting an open state of an output terminal, and an abnormality detection circuit and an overheat protection circuit for detecting a short-circuit state are provided, an operating state of each circuit can be output to the outside with a small number of external terminals, and an increase in chip size can be suppressed.

Another object of the present invention is to provide a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator (regulator IC) capable of detecting an abnormality such as an open circuit or a short circuit of a load connected to an output terminal without using a detection resistor, and capable of arbitrarily setting a current value for detecting an abnormality such as an open circuit or a short circuit of a load connected to an output terminal in accordance with an applicable system.

In order to achieve the above object, the present invention provides a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator including a voltage control transistor connected between a voltage input terminal to which a dc voltage is input and an output terminal, and a control circuit for controlling the voltage control transistor based on an output feedback voltage, the semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator including:

an opening abnormality detection circuit that detects an open state of the output terminal;

a short-circuit abnormality detection circuit that detects a short-circuit state of the output terminal;

a first output terminal for outputting a detection result of the opening abnormality detection circuit to the outside;

a second output terminal for outputting a detection result of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit to the outside; and

an overheat protection circuit for detecting a temperature of a semiconductor substrate forming the semiconductor integrated circuit and turning off the voltage control transistor by the control circuit when the temperature of the semiconductor substrate is detected to be higher than or equal to a predetermined temperature set in advance,

the second output terminal outputs a signal obtained by logical or of the output signal of the overheat protection circuit and the output signal of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit, and the output signal of the open abnormality detection circuit is not blocked by the output signal of the overheat protection circuit.

According to the semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator having the above configuration, since the open state and the short-circuit state of the output terminal are detected and the detection signal is output to the outside, the load on the control device (CPU) such as a personal computer of the control system can be reduced.

In the semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator, the second output terminal outputs a signal obtained by taking the logical or of the output of the overheat protection circuit and the output of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit as the short-circuit abnormality signal, and therefore, it is possible to avoid a situation in which the operations of detecting and releasing the short circuit are repeated and a plurality of detection pulses are added to the detection signal.

In addition, the number of external terminals can be reduced as compared with a case where the output of the overheat protection circuit and the output of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit are output through different external terminals.

Further, since the configuration is such that the first output terminal for outputting the detection result of the open abnormality detection circuit to the outside is provided, and the output of the open abnormality detection circuit is not blocked by the output of the overheat protection circuit, it is possible to determine whether the short-circuit abnormality detection signal rises due to an overcurrent in which the overheat protection circuit is not operating or whether the short-circuit abnormality detection signal rises due to occurrence of a complete short circuit by a control device such as a personal Computer (CPU).

It is preferable here to make up that,

the disclosed device is provided with: a first transistor and a second transistor which are provided in parallel with the voltage control transistor and through which a current in a reduced proportion to a current flowing through the voltage control transistor flows,

the opening abnormality detection circuit includes: a first voltage comparison circuit for comparing a voltage obtained by converting a current flowing through the first transistor with a predetermined comparison voltage to determine a magnitude of the current,

the short circuit abnormality detection circuit includes: a second voltage comparison circuit for comparing a voltage obtained by converting a current flowing through the second transistor with a predetermined comparison voltage to determine a magnitude of the current,

when a current smaller than a preset opening abnormality detection current value flows through the first transistor, an output signal of the first voltage comparison circuit is inverted, and when a current larger than a preset short circuit abnormality detection current value flows through the second transistor, an output signal of the second voltage comparison circuit is inverted.

According to the above configuration, since the abnormality of the open or short circuit of the load connected to the output terminal is detected based on the current proportional to the current flowing through the voltage control transistor, that is, without using the detection resistor for detecting the output current, the detection of the open abnormality can be detected with higher accuracy than the case of providing the detection resistor having a low resistance at the input terminal.

Further, it is preferable that a delay circuit for delaying at least an output of the second voltage comparison circuit out of outputs of the first voltage comparison circuit and the second voltage comparison circuit is provided, and a signal obtained by taking a logical and of an output signal of the second voltage comparison circuit and a signal delayed by the delay circuit is outputted as the short-circuit abnormality detection signal through the second output terminal.

Thus, it is possible to prevent an inrush current from flowing into a capacitor connected to the output terminal at the start of operation and an erroneous output of the short-circuit abnormality detection signal.

Further, it is preferable that the apparatus comprises:

a first external terminal to which a current-voltage conversion element for converting a current flowing through the first transistor into a voltage is connected;

a second external terminal to which a current-voltage conversion element for converting a current flowing through the second transistor into a voltage is connected,

the first voltage comparison circuit compares a voltage converted by the current-voltage conversion element connected to the first external terminal with a predetermined comparison voltage, and the second voltage comparison circuit compares a voltage converted by the current-voltage conversion element connected to the second external terminal with a predetermined comparison voltage.

According to the above configuration, the current value to be a criterion for determining an open abnormality and the current value to be a criterion for determining a short-circuit abnormality can be arbitrarily and accurately set according to the system.

According to the present invention, in a semiconductor integrated circuit (regulator IC) constituting a dc power supply device such as a series regulator, when an abnormality detection circuit for detecting an open state of an output terminal, an abnormality detection circuit for detecting a short-circuit state, and an overheat protection circuit are provided, it is possible to output an operating state of each circuit to the outside with a small number of external terminals and suppress an increase in chip size. Further, the regulator IC can detect an abnormality such as an open or short circuit of a load connected to the output terminal without using a detection resistor, and can set a current value for detecting an abnormality such as an open or short circuit of a load connected to the output terminal as desired according to an applicable system.

Description of reference numerals

10: regulator IC, 11: error amplifier, 12: reference voltage circuit, 13: bias circuit, 14: current mirror circuit, 15: overheat protection circuit, 16: open abnormality detection comparator, 17: short-circuit abnormality detection comparator, 19: delay circuit, Q1: voltage control transistor, Q2 to Q4: a current mirror transistor.

Detailed Description

Preferred embodiments of the present invention will be described below with reference to the accompanying drawings.

Fig. 1 shows an embodiment of a series regulator as a dc power supply device to which the present invention is applied. In fig. 1, a portion surrounded by a chain line is formed as a semiconductor integrated circuit (regulator IC)10 on a single crystal silicon semiconductor chip, and a capacitor Co is connected to an output terminal (OUT) of the regulator IC10 to function as a dc power supply device for supplying a stable dc voltage.

IN the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment, as shown IN fig. 1, a voltage control transistor Q1 formed of a PNP bipolar transistor is connected between a voltage input terminal (IN) to which a dc voltage Vin is applied and an output terminal (OUT), and bleeder resistors R1 and R2 for dividing the output voltage Vout are connected IN series between the output terminal (OUT) and a ground to which a ground potential GND is applied.

The voltage VFB divided by the bleeder resistors R1 and R2 is fed back to the non-inverting input terminal of the error amplifier 11 serving as the error amplifying circuit for controlling the base terminal of the voltage control transistor Q1. Then, the error amplifier 11 controls the voltage control transistor Q1 based on the potential difference between the output feedback voltage VFB and the predetermined reference voltage Vref, and controls the output voltage Vout to a desired potential.

The regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is provided with a reference voltage circuit 12 for generating a reference voltage Vref to be applied to the inverting input terminal of the error amplifier 11, a bias circuit 13 for causing an operating current to flow through the error amplifier 11 or the reference voltage circuit 12, a current limiting circuit 14 connected to the base terminal of the voltage control transistor Q1 for limiting an output current, and an overheat protection circuit 15 for stopping the operation of the error amplifier 11 and turning off the transistor Q1 when the temperature of the chip rises to a predetermined temperature or higher.

The reference voltage circuit 12 may be formed of a resistor, a zener diode, and the like connected in series. The bias circuit 13 is provided with a function of supplying or cutting off a bias current to the error amplifier 11 in accordance with a control signal Cont input to the external terminal CNT from a personal Computer (CPU) or the like outside the chip. When the output current increases and the output voltage decreases due to a load abnormality or the like, and the base voltage of the error amplifier 11 decreases in order to flow a larger amount of current through the transistor Q1, the current limiting circuit 14 limits the current by clamping so that the base current does not become larger than a predetermined value.

Further, in the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment, a transistor Q1 for voltage control is provided in parallel, Q1 and bipolar transistors Q2, Q3, and Q4 constituting a current mirror circuit are provided, and the same voltage as the voltage applied to the base terminal of the transistor Q1 for voltage control is applied to the base terminals as the control terminals of the transistors Q2 to Q4. Thus, a current (1/N current) proportional to the collector current of Q1 flows through Q2 to Q4 according to the size ratio N of the elements. The transistor Q1 is formed by connecting N transistors of the same size in parallel, and when each of Q2 to Q4 is formed by 1 transistor, it is set that a current proportional to the number of elements flows.

The regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is provided with an external terminal P1 for connecting to a resistor Rop for current-voltage conversion outside the chip, and an external terminal P2 for connecting to a resistor Rsc, the collector terminal of the current mirror transistor Q2 being connected to the external terminal P1, and the collector terminal of the current mirror transistor Q3 being connected to the external terminal P2. Further, a comparator 16 for detecting an open abnormality having an inverting input terminal connected to the external terminal P1 and a reference voltage Vref 'applied to a non-inverting input terminal, and a comparator 17 for detecting a short circuit having a non-inverting input terminal connected to the external terminal P2 and a reference voltage Vref' applied to an inverting input terminal are provided.

When an abnormal-opening detection current of, for example, 10mA flows through the voltage-controlling transistor Q1, the external resistor Rop is set to have a resistance value such that the voltage between both terminals of the resistor becomes equal to the reference voltage Vref'. On the other hand, when a short-circuit abnormality detection current of, for example, 200mA flows through the voltage control transistor Q1, the external resistor Rsc is set to have a resistance value such that the voltage between the terminals of the resistor becomes the same value as the reference voltage Vref'.

As described above, in the present embodiment, since the current values for detecting the open abnormality and the short-circuit abnormality are set by the external resistors Rop and Rsc, the detected current values (threshold values) can be arbitrarily set according to the system to be used, and the same voltage value can be used as the reference voltage Vref' for the comparators 16 and 17, and the circuit for generating the reference voltage can be simplified.

The regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is provided with an NPN transistor Q5 in which the output terminal of the comparator 16 is connected to the base terminal, an OR gate 18 in which the output of the comparator 17 and the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 are input, and an NPN transistor Q6 of a transistor Q6 in which the output terminal of the OR gate 18 is connected to the base terminal. Further, external terminals P3 and P4 for outputting a signal to an external CPU or the like in the form of an open collector are provided in the regulator IC chip, the collector terminal of the transistor Q5 is connected to the external terminal P3, and the collector terminal of the transistor Q6 is connected to the external terminal P4.

Next, the operation of the regulator IC10 according to the present embodiment will be described with reference to the timing chart of fig. 2. In fig. 2, the left half period T1 indicates the timing when the regulator is turned on after performing a steady operation for a period of time after the start of the operation of the regulator, and the right half period T2 indicates the timing when the regulator is short-circuited after performing a steady operation for a period of time after the start of the operation of the regulator.

As shown in fig. 2, if the input voltage Vin rises at a timing t1 and the signal Cont of the control terminal CNT changes from the outside to the high level at a timing t2, the regulator IC10 starts operating, and the output voltage Vout rises and is controlled to a predetermined voltage. In the transition period until the output voltage Vout rises, a rush circuit (surge current) flows to the capacitor Co connected to the output terminal, and then a constant current flows in accordance with the state of the load (period Ta).

Then, in this steady operation state, if an abnormality occurs in which the output terminal is open, the output current Iout decreases rapidly (timing t 3). Then, the current flowing through the current mirror transistor Q2 also decreases, so the comparator 16 detects this and its output becomes high level. As a result, the transistor Q5 is turned on, the signal Err-OP output from the external terminal P3 becomes low level, and the CPU that obtains this signal can detect that an opening abnormality has occurred. If the CPU detects an open abnormality, the control signal Cont is made low, thereby stopping the action of the regulator IC10 (timing t 4).

After that, if the abnormal open state is eliminated, when the control signal Cont becomes high at the timing t5, the regulator IC10 resumes operation, and the output voltage Vout rises to a predetermined voltage. At this time, although the rush current flows in the transient period until the output voltage Vout rises, the constant current flows thereafter in accordance with the state of the load (period Tb).

Then, if a short circuit occurs in the load in this steady operation state, the output current Iout increases sharply (timing t 6). Then, the current flowing through the current mirror transistor Q3 also increases, so the comparator 17 detects this and its output becomes high level. As a result, the transistor Q6 turns on, the signal Err-SC output from the external terminal P4 becomes low level, and the CPU that obtains this signal can detect that a short-circuit abnormality has occurred.

However, in the case of a short-circuit abnormality, since heat is generated by large electric power as the output current Iout increases rapidly, the overheat protection circuit stops the operation of the error amplifier 11 and turns off the transistor Q1 when the chip temperature rises to a predetermined temperature, thereby turning off the output current Iout and canceling the detection of the short-circuit state. If the temperature of the heat-dissipating semiconductor chip is lowered, the shutdown is released, and if the short-circuit state is maintained, the operation of detecting and outputting the short-circuit state is repeated, and a failure occurs as a short-circuit abnormality detection signal.

Therefore, the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is provided with an or gate 18 that takes the logic between the output of the comparator 17 and the output of the overheat protection circuit 15, and the transistor Q6 is turned on/off by the output of the or gate 18. In this way, if a short-circuit abnormality occurs and the output current Iout increases rapidly, the short-circuit abnormality detection signal is output, and the transistor Q6 is turned on/off by the logical or between the output of the comparator 17 and the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 so that the short-circuit abnormality detection signal is maintained even when the chip temperature rises and the output of the overheat protection circuit detects a high temperature, whereby the short-circuit abnormality detection signal of the regulator IC10 can be prevented from falling into the above-described repetitive operation. Then, if the CPU detects a short-circuit abnormality, the control signal Cont is set to a low level, thereby stopping the operation of the regulator IC10 (timing t 7).

As described above, although the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment has a rush current flowing after the start of the operation of the regulator IC10, and the output of the rush current comparator 17 becomes high and turns on the transistor Q6, and Err-SC becomes low, the dead band program for performing the ignoring process can be executed on the CPU side that obtains the error detection signal in response to the short-circuit detection pulse after the power-on.

In a device provided with the overheat protection circuit 15 and the open abnormality detection circuit (comparator 16) as in the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment, if the overheat protection circuit 15 operates, the control transistor Q1 and the current mirror transistor Q2 are turned off, and the output of the comparator 16 is inverted to output the open abnormality detection signal Err _ OP. Therefore, an external personal Computer (CPU) that obtains the signal may erroneously determine that an open abnormality has occurred.

Therefore, for example, in the IC of fig. 1, a logic gate such as an and gate that outputs a detection signal for turning off the opening abnormality detection circuit (comparator 16) if the overheat protection circuit 15 is operating, and an inverter for inverting the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 are provided, and the output of the inverter is applied to one input terminal of the and gate. As a result, as shown in fig. 6, when the output TSD of the overheat protection circuit rises (during a high level period), the detection signal Err _ OP for turning on the abnormality detection circuit is generally not output (the detection level does not change) (see a portion surrounded by a chain line denoted by a in fig. 6). In general, the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 and the detection signal of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit (comparator 17) are output from the respective external terminals, and the detection signal Err _ SC in fig. 6 indicates the signal timing when configured as described above.

In contrast, in the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment, a signal Err _ SC that is a logical or between the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 and the detection signal of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit (17) is output from the external terminal P4. Therefore, the number of external terminals can be reduced compared to the case where the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 and the detection signal of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit (17) are separately output. However, when the detection level of the short-circuit abnormality detection is set low and an overcurrent that does not operate the overheat protection circuit 15 flows, a current that is large to some extent flows due to a short circuit of the load, and thus the chip temperature may increase and the overheat protection circuit 15 may operate. At this time, if the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 and the detection signal of the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit (17) are output from 1 external terminal P4, the external Computer (CPU) cannot determine whether the overheat protection circuit 15 is operating and the detection signal Err _ SC is rising or whether the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit (17) detects an overcurrent in which the overheat protection circuit 15 is not operating and the detection signal Err _ SC is rising.

However, in the above-described embodiment, as shown in the timing chart of fig. 2, even when the output TSD of the overheat protection circuit 15 rises (during a high level), if the opening abnormality detection circuit (16) detects an opening abnormality, the detection signal Err _ OP is output, and therefore it is possible to determine by the external Computer (CPU) whether the detection signal Err _ SC rises due to an overcurrent in which the overheat protection circuit 15 is not operating, or whether the detection signal Err _ SC rises due to occurrence of a complete short circuit.

That is, in the above-described embodiment, in the case of a dead short, since the overheat protection circuit 15 must operate and the open abnormality detection signal Err _ OP should change after the short abnormality detection signal Err _ SC rises, the external personal Computer (CPU) can distinguish between the occurrence of an accidental overcurrent and the occurrence of a dead short by monitoring the Err _ SC of the external terminal P4 and the signal Err _ OP of the external terminal P3. Therefore, as shown in the section from t6 to t7 in fig. 2, it is possible to perform different handling processes when a preset overcurrent is detected and when a large amount of heat is radiated in accordance with the operation of the overheat protection circuit. As a result, for example, it is possible to avoid an erroneous operation in which the regulator is turned off by erroneously determining that a sudden overcurrent has occurred as a complete short circuit.

(modification example)

Next, a modification of the regulator IC of the above embodiment will be described with reference to fig. 3 and 4.

Fig. 3 shows a regulator IC of a first modification example thereof. In this modification, in order to prevent an erroneous detection signal due to the rush current, a delay circuit 19 including the resistance, the capacitance, and the like of the outputs of the delay comparators 16 and 17, a NOR (NOR) gate 20 for taking the logical or of the outputs of the comparators 16 and 17 and inputting the logical or to the delay circuit 19, and gates 21 and 22 for taking the logical and between the output of the delay circuit 19 and the outputs of the original comparators 16 and 17 before the delay are provided in the regulator IC 10.

The regulator IC of the above embodiment determines that a short-circuit state occurs based on a case where a relatively large current flows to the output terminal. On the other hand, at the time of IC start-up, a relatively large rush current (surge current) flows to the capacitor Co of the output terminal. However, since the regulator IC of fig. 1 cannot distinguish the rush current from the current flowing to the output terminal when the short-circuit abnormality occurs, it is possible to avoid the occurrence of an erroneous detection pulse accompanying the detection of the rush current Ir in the output of the comparator 17 as shown in the timing chart of fig. 2.

In contrast, in the system using the regulator IC of the present modification, a configuration is adopted in which an erroneous detection signal accompanying the detection of the inrush current does not occur. Thus, there is an advantage that it is not necessary to set a dead band program in the CPU of the subsequent stage.

Specifically, the delay circuit 19 includes a constant current source IC0, a capacitor C1 charged by the constant current source IC0, a resistor R4 connected in series between a connection node N1 between the constant current source IC0 and the capacitor C1 and a ground point, a switching transistor Qs, and a comparator CMP, and the output voltage of the nor gate 20 is input to a base terminal of the transistor Qs. Further, an external terminal P5 connected to the connection node N1 is provided, and the delay time can be increased without increasing the chip size by connecting an external capacitor Cd to the terminal P5.

In a normal operation state in which both outputs of the comparators 16 and 17 are at a low level, the delay circuit 19 is turned on by applying a high level to the base terminal of the transistor Qs through the output of the nor gate 20, and the capacitors C1 and Cd are discharged. Then, the comparator 16 detects an open state or the comparator 17 detects a short-circuit state, and if the output of either one of the comparators becomes high, the output of the nor gate 20 becomes low and the transistor Qs turns off.

Then, the capacitors C1 and Cd are gradually charged, and the potential of the connection node N1 gradually rises. And if the potential of the connection node N1 becomes higher than the reference voltage Vref1 of the comparator CMP after a predetermined time elapses, the output of the comparator CMP changes from the low level to the high level. When the on state is detected, the output of the and gate 21 becomes high, the transistor Q5 is turned on, and the external terminal P3 becomes low from high.

When a short-circuit abnormality is detected, the output of the and gate 22 goes high, the transistor Q6 is turned on, and the external terminal P4 goes from high to low. The delay time of the delay circuit 19 is set to be slightly longer than the period in which the rush current Ir shown in fig. 2 flows.

By providing the delay circuit 19, the comparator CMP, and the and gates 21 and 22, the error detection pulse accompanying the detection of the rush current does not occur in the present modification.

In fig. 3, the delay circuit 19 delays the outputs of the comparators 16 and 17, respectively, but only the output of the comparator 17 for short-circuit abnormality detection may be delayed. Also, the nor gate 20 and the and gate 21 of fig. 3 are not required in this case.

Fig. 4 shows a regulator IC of a second modification. This modification also serves as the short-circuit abnormality detection comparator 17 and the comparator constituting the current limiting circuit 14 in the embodiment of fig. 1. Therefore, in this case, the current mirror transistor Q3 through which the monitor current for detecting the short-circuit abnormality flows and the current mirror transistor Q4 through which the monitor current of the current limiting circuit 14 flows can be used in combination.

Specifically, the current mirror transistor Q4 and the external terminal P2 in fig. 1 are omitted, an internal resistor R4 for converting the current of the current mirror transistor Q3 into a voltage is provided, and the voltage converted by the resistor R4 is input to the non-inverting input terminal of the comparator 17 for detecting a short-circuit abnormality. The output of the comparator 17 and the output of the overheat protection circuit 15 are input to the base terminal of the output transistor Q6 via the OR gate 18.

On the other hand, the output of the comparator 17 is applied to the base terminals of the voltage control transistor Q1, the current mirror transistors Q2, Q3 via the inverters 23, 24, and if a current of a predetermined current value or more flows through the voltage control transistor Q1, the voltage control transistor Q1 is current-clamped to limit the output current Iout.

The regulator IC according to the second modification has the following advantages: the number of one external terminal can be reduced as compared with the regulator IC of the embodiment of fig. 1, and the short-circuit abnormality detection circuit can be used as a current limiting circuit as well, so that the chip can be miniaturized.

As a configuration for using both the short-circuit abnormality detection comparator 17 and the comparator constituting the current limiting circuit 14, a configuration may be adopted in which the external terminal P2 is provided and the resistor R4 is connected as an external resistor, so that the detected current value (threshold value) can be adjusted.

The invention made by the present inventors has been specifically described above based on examples, but the present invention is not limited to the above examples.
